result: The authors characterize the laminar distribution of GABA+ and PV+ neurons in marmoset V1, finding that both GABA+ and PV+ cell density peaks in layers 2/3 and 4C, with PV+ cells representing on average 61% of all GABAergic cells. These distributions differ from mouse V1 where peaks occur in layers 4 and 5, and are consistent with previous studies in macaque and marmoset V1.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge this contribution, with one stating 'the authors characterize the laminar distribution pattern of GABA+ and PV+ cells in V1. This survey may prove valuable to researchers.' Another reviewer notes this provides 'a rigorous survey of the laminar distributions of GABA+ and PV+ neurons in marmoset V1 which has value independent of the viral injections.' No concerns were raised about these findings.

result: The authors tested three serotypes (AAV1, AAV7, AAV9) of the h56D promoter-AAV for targeting GABAergic neurons, finding that AAV9 showed the highest specificity (82.3% ± 1.1) and coverage (66.1% ± 3.9) across all layers, though specificity and coverage varied by serotype and cortical layer. AAV7 showed layer-specific expression biased toward superficial and deep layers.
evaluation: Reviewers raised significant concerns about the reliability of these findings. One reviewer noted 'The three different serotypes of AAV expressing reporter under the h56D promoter were only tested once each, and all in the same animal. There are many variables that can contribute to the success (or failure) of a viral injection, so observations with an n = 1 cannot be considered reliable.' Another reviewer stated the 'data set is small. Which of the results would hold up had a larger number of injections been made into a larger number of marmosets remains unclear.' After revision, one reviewer noted 'the new language to qualify the strength of evidence relating to the interpretation of the data relating to the 3 different serotypes of virus used to test h56D is appropriate,' suggesting the authors acknowledged these limitations.

result: The authors demonstrate that AAV-PHP.eB-S5E2 induces transgene expression in PV cells with up to 98% specificity and 86-90% coverage depending on layer, with optimal results obtained using injection volumes of 150-300 nl. The laminar distribution of viral expression matched that of PV+ immunohistochemistry.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly supported this finding. One reviewer stated 'A second contribution is the demonstration that AAV-S5E2 drives transgene expression selectively in parvalbumin-expressing neurons when vectors are delivered intraparenchymally (the study introducing AAV-S5E2 used intravenous injections).' Another reviewer noted 'Federer et al. further validate the utility of S5E2 as a PV-selective enhancer in NHPs.' The editor's summary stated the study 'carefully characteriz[es] the laminar expression profile' of S5E2 for 'parvalbumin+ cell-type selective expression.' No concerns were raised about these PV-specific findings.

result: The authors found that both GABA- and PV-specific AAVs significantly reduced GABA and PV immunoreactivity at viral injection sites (20-33% reduction), with each virus showing greater reduction of its target marker. This suggests actual viral specificity may be higher than measured.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly highlighted this as a strength. One reviewer stated 'A strength of this study is the analysis of marker gene expression at AAV injection sites. Some endogenous genes are difficult to detect following AAV injections, which is an important observation.' No concerns were raised about these findings, and reviewers treated this as a valuable methodological contribution.

result: The authors conclude that these viral vectors are promising tools for studying GABA and PV cell function and connectivity in primate cortex.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed this conclusion. One stated 'A major goal of this study was to quantify the specificity and coverage of AAV-h56D and AAV-S5E2 vectors in marmoset cortex. This goal was achieved. This report provides a valuable guide for other investigators using these tools.' The editor noted the study 'provides a valuable building block' and 'contributes solid evidence to our understanding of these tools.' The overall assessment was that despite limitations in sample size, the tools were validated for use.

result: The laminar distribution of reporter protein expression mediated by the GABA- and PV-enhancer AAVs resembles the laminar distribution of GABA+ and PV+ cells revealed by immunohistochemistry in marmoset V1.
evaluation: This finding is implicitly supported by reviewers who noted the study 'carefully characteriz[es] the laminar expression profile' and provides 'a rigorous survey' of these distributions. The match between viral expression and immunohistochemistry is central to validating the viral tools, and no concerns were raised about this correspondence.
